did_you_know.text: The battle between Israel and the Philistines took place on Mount Gilboa. During the battle, the Israelites fled, and many of them were killed.
The three sons of Saul who were killed in the battle were Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
Saul was severely wounded by the archers, and the text describes the battle against him as very fierce.
Saul asked his armor-bearer to kill him so that he would not fall into the hands of the Philistines and be abused by them, but the armor-bearer was afraid and refused.
When his armor-bearer refused, Saul fell on his sword. When the armor-bearer saw this, he also fell on his sword and died.
When the Israelites in the valley saw that they had been defeated and that Saul and his sons had died, they abandoned their cities, and the Philistines settled in them.
The Philistines stripped Saul, took his head and his armor, and sent them throughout their land to announce their victory.
Saul’s armor was placed in the temple of the Philistine gods, and his skull was fastened in the temple of Dagon.
The men of Jabesh-gilead brought back the bodies of Saul and his sons, buried their bones under the oak at Jabesh, and fasted for seven days.

The text explains Saul’s downfall as resulting from his unfaithfulness to the LORD, his failure to keep the LORD’s word, and his consulting a medium. Afterward, the kingship was given to David son of Jesse.
